messages.subject: BART stan codes - prob of bursting and balloon colours
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm wondering if anyone has used this for the BART, as I have a few questions. The paper that's cited in the documentation and the Wallsten et al., 2005 papers are helpful, but I'm still confused about certain things (whether probability of bursting is stationary, whether balloons of different colours and probabilities are used, and whether anyone has incorporated that, if not). I've already edited the stan codes of some of the other tasks, so I have some experience in doing that, but I first wanted to check if anyone has had experience with the BART specifically.

Thanks so much!

Zoe

messages.author: f9eb43b98f013da6
messages.subject: Re: BART stan codes - prob of bursting and balloon colours
parts:
Hi Zoe,

I'm the graduate student who contributed to the BART code to the hBayesDM. I'm glad you're using the package for your research.

The bart_par4 model is based on the original BART paradigm (Lejuez et al., 2002). In the original BART paradigm, the probability of bursting changes over pumps and only one kind of balloon is used. So, as you know, you have to modify the Stan file if you want to use our code to the experiment setting you proposed.

In the Stan code, 'p_burst' indicates the participant's belief about the probability of bursting. If the participant is not informed of the probability structure, the participant would start with his/her prior belief and learns the probability of bursting by trials and errors. I think the equations of the model remain the same whether the probability of bursting is stationary or not. To deal with balloons of different colors and probabilities, I think you need to define independent values for each balloon (n_succ, n_pump, p_burst, etc).

I'm not sure if I understood your question correctly, but please feel free to let me know if you have more questions.

Best,
Harhim
